lines.text: The thermometer says 9. Your face will say 4. I go with your face.
You'll want the winter coat {WHEN}. || Yes, the number looks fine. The number isn't going outside.
It feels colder than it is. I can't feel a thing, and I'm still right.
It's this cold the whole day. || I dress you by 'feels like'. The thermometer just reads; I sympathize.
The thermometer says mild. The wind didn't get the memo.
Nobody believes 'feels like' until they're outside. I believe it from in here.
The cold sets in {WHEN}, so pack a hat, scarf and gloves. || The thermometer will look reasonable. The wind won't be.
A sweater won't do {WHEN}, so bring a jacket. || The real number is for bragging. The 'feels like' is for going outside.
Rain is possible {WHENP}. An umbrella could help. || Your app gives it a percentage so it can't be wrong. I give advice.
Your phone now predicts rain. While it's raining. Visionary.
I do one thing. Your phone does weather between ads.
This outfit works all day. || Check your phone if you like. It'll say the same thing, with an ad.
It's this cold the whole day. || Your phone agrees. It just took four taps to say so.
Your phone shows ten days ahead. I show today, and I get it right.
What you're wearing works for the rest of the evening. || No need to ask your phone. It'll only ask you to rate it.
Your app said 40%. I said umbrella. One of us is on the wall for a reason.
It's this cold the whole day. || 'Cold enough for you?' is a forecast too. Just a lazy one.
Strangers will say 'nice day, huh?' like it's news. I published it this morning.
This outfit works all day. || Strangers will tell you it's nice out. Amateurs. I've been on it since six.
Strangers talk weather to fill silence. I talk weather because it's my job.
Hot all day: drink water and find shade. || 'Hot enough for you?' Every stranger, all day. I said it once.
Nice out. That's your whole conversation with the neighbors sorted.
Everyone's a weather expert in an elevator. I'm one on a wall, full time.
Dressed right for the rest of the evening. || Run out of things to say tonight? The weather was fine. You're welcome.
April showers. Folk wisdom nailed one month and retired.
Pack the umbrella. Rain sets in {WHENP} and doesn't let up. || Cows lie down before rain, apparently. I don't need cows.
Rain is possible {WHENP}. An umbrella could help. || Grandpa's knee says rain too. I have better data and no knee.
Snow moves in {WHENP}. || Folk wisdom would need a woolly caterpillar for this. I need Wi-Fi.
A short shower comes {WHENP}. Bring the umbrella. || Red sky at night, sailor's delight. Sailors didn't have me.
Rain before seven, dry by eleven? Cute rhyme. I'll take it from here.
There's no dry spell today. Bring the umbrella. || April showers bring May flowers. Your shoes don't care about May.
Take the umbrella for now. The rain stops {WHENSTOP}. || No rhyme for that. Just me, being accurate.
Dark since half past four. The day clocked out before you did.
What you're wearing works for the rest of the evening. || Yes, 'evening'. At five. I checked the date. Not my fault.
Dark by half past four, and I don't even light up. Good luck.
Nothing changes tonight. || It's been 'evening' since half past four. Night is just more of it.
The sun's on half days until February. I'm still on full shifts.
Pitch dark, and dinner's still hours away. That's winter for you.
What you're wearing works for the rest of the evening. || It's a long one. Sunset at 4:30 will do that.
It's been dark for hours. It's not even six.
Freezing. Somewhere, a man in shorts is telling everyone he runs hot.

lines.text: You can take the jacket off {WHEN}. || The shorts guy never had one on. He'll want you to know.

lines.text: I dress everyone for the cold. The guy in shorts never checks me.

lines.text: Too hot? Last week everyone begged for this. I have the forecasts to prove it.

lines.text: It gets hot {WHEN}, so bring water. || Everyone wanted summer. Nobody asked for the afternoon.

lines.text: Summer, exactly as ordered. No refunds, no exchanges.

lines.text: Last month: 'when's summer coming?' Now: 'too hot.' I don't take requests.

lines.text: {WHEN} you'll want a sweater. || Pumpkin spice showed up in August. I wait for actual weather.
Fall weather. Pumpkin spice will take the credit. I did the forecast.
This outfit works all day. || No pumpkin in the forecast. It's in everything else.
Cool enough for a sweater. Barely cool enough for pumpkin spice.
A sweater won't do {WHEN}, so bring a jacket. || Fall is finally here. Pumpkin spice is on its second lap.
This outfit works all day. || Pumpkin spice declared fall weeks ago. I go by the temperature.
Sweater weather at last. The pumpkin spice has been waiting since August.
It's this cold the whole day. || Pumpkin spice season, apparently. It's not seasoning the weather.
